title: Average cost bounded by worst-case cost
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\\Omega$ be a finite nonempty input alphabet with probability distribution $\\pi$, let $\\alpha$ be an output set, and let $f:\\Omega^n\\to\\alpha$. For any randomized decision tree $T$ computing $f$, its average query cost under independent inputs drawn from $\\pi$ is at most its worst-case query cost over all inputs.
hypotheses_covered: $\\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\\Omega$
$T$ is a randomized decision tree computing $f$
